title: The Weird Circle
identity_notes: Transcribed New York literary horror/mystery anthology of 78 programs, distributed in syndication rather than as one simultaneous nationwide network schedule. Frozen GRH contains the complete numbered package; #33 and #64 lack dates/numbers in the production catalog but are recoverable from the documented sequence.

eras.notes: The Weird Circle was produced as transcription blocks for syndication; local broadcast dates varied by market.

historical_context.title: AFM recording ban and The Weird Circle music-free sound
historical_context.description: Schadow documents that the 1942 American Federation of Musicians recording ban kept music out of the transcribed series; later episodes retained the music-free sound for uniformity.

historical_context.title: Classic-literature adaptation culture
historical_context.description: The anthology relied heavily on older literary sources, especially Gothic, supernatural and macabre fiction.

historical_context.title: Transcribed syndication model
historical_context.description: The Weird Circle was produced as transcription packages and licensed to stations/markets, so local air dates varied rather than following one national live-network clock.

historical_context.title: Wartime-era escapist horror anthology
historical_context.description: The package circulated during World War II while drawing most stories from earlier literature rather than contemporary war plots.
